source_policy: HeroBloks is useful for custom/compatible discovery and source labels, not manufacturing metrology.
Retailer compatibility claims are hypotheses until tested.
BrickLink inventory evidence can establish official component relationships, but physical dimensions for printing still require measurement/validated geometry.
Images are evidence for morphology and family candidates, not precise joint dimensions.
Maker identity and serial prefix are priors only; classify the mechanical architecture at release/body-family level.
Alternate lower bodies are not only cosmetic variants when they change footprint, articulation, component graph or surface topology.
MegaFig is a source/scale label, not a mechanical standard; documented heights span multiple very-large scales and makers.
Ball-joint arms can be a joint architecture variant at standard minifigure scale; exact adapter geometry remains maker/release specific until measured.
Cross-franchise use of BigFig terminology further confirms that the term is a market morphology label rather than an official single connector standard.
Same maker and same character can have different size/body products: Renzaima currently has War Machine Mk 1 records at 8 cm and 4.3 cm, reinforcing release-level classification.
